ai.title: Add allowlisted reposnapshot telemetry column
ai.summary: New `repo_snapshot` column added to `ChatCompletionTraceRow` and populated in `sdk/src/run.ts` via `toRepoSnapshot` projection. Explicit allowlist in `common/src/util/file.ts` restricts telemetry to aggregate scalars, preventing legacy `gitChanges` fields like `status` and `diff` from leaking raw patch content. `REPO_SNAPSHOT_FIELDS` excludes branch names and file paths, enforcing contract compliance for repository scale metrics. Empty or undefined snapshots return `undefined` rather than null rows to distinguish unmeasured states.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant in a software project, it now quietly records a small, safe summary of your repository, like how many files it has and roughly how active it is, instead of sending sensitive details such as branch names or file paths. This summary is stripped down to only aggregate numbers and counts, with a strict allowlist preventing any raw patch content, code changes, or identifying names from being transmitted. The feature is live today and applies to all SDK users whose projects generate telemetry, ensuring repository scale metrics are captured without risking source code or private repository information leaking into analytics.

ai.title: CLI think tag parser fixes orphan close tags and block merging
ai.summary: Refactored `think-tag-parser.ts` to handle orphan `</think>` tags by pushing preceding text as thinking segments. `block-operations.ts` simplified `appendTextWithThinkParsingToBlocks` by merging last block content with new text before checking for think tags, replacing complex partial tag logic. This ensures correct block splitting when think tags span multiple text chunks. No user-facing command changes.

eli5.text: When the assistant writes a response, it sometimes tucks thoughts into hidden tags that look like parentheses with a 'think' label, the opening and closing of those tags can arrive split across separate pieces of text. The software that reassembled those pieces was misreading the splits, which could drop stray closing tags or glue text together wrongly, so the reconstructed message came out garbled. The fix teaches the parser to treat a lone closing tag as its own boundary, and tells the text-joining step to blend consecutive pieces first before hunting for tags, so each tag pair stays intact and the assembled output keeps its intended structure. This works today for everything you see in the CLI; there are no new commands or settings to use.

ai.title: First-party ad views get resilient acknowledgement transport
ai.summary: A new acknowledgement module in `@codebuff/common/ads/first-party-view-ack` records first-party ad impressions with a best-effort retry sequence: three attempts at a two-second timeout each with 250ms and 1s bounded delays, retrying only server errors, timeouts, and network failures, never 4xx responses. The CLI's `useGravityAd` hook now dispatches this transport only for `first_party` providers, leaving third-party ads on the legacy pixel path, and surfaces observations as the operational-only event `ads.first_party_view_ack` through a server-validated telemetry allowlist that rejects any unknown fields. The landing-screen ad banner now orders ads by canonical request order via `orderedRequestedAds` and reads visible waiting-room placements from a new `waiting-room-placements.ts` module instead of the local `MIN_CARD_WIDTH` constant.
ai.evidence: New module `common/src/ads/first-party-view-ack.ts` defines `acknowledgeFirstPartyView`, retry delays, and outcome constants, and is wired into impression recording in `cli/src/hooks/use-gravity-ad.ts` via `dispatchFirstPartyViewAcknowledgement`, with telemetry validation added in `common/src/util/axiom-only-log.ts` and a new `AnalyticsEvent.ADS_FIRST_PARTY_VIEW_ACK` event in `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`.

ai.title: Disable nodemodules caching on Linux CI jobs
ai.summary: Dependency caching disabled for Linux CI jobs in `docs/testing.md` after cold `bun install` proved 7-8s faster per job than warm cache restores on Ubicloud runners. This change applies to `setup-project` and standalone Ubicloud workflows, while Windows and macOS caches remain active pending similar measurements. Small caches for `sdk/dist`, Next.js builds, and the Bun runtime are retained due to favorable transfer-to-compute ratios.

eli5.text: On Linux computers, the software stopped saving and reusing downloaded helper packages between test runs; instead it grabs a fresh copy each time, which the team found actually finished tests faster. If you run checks on Linux machines, your jobs start a little sooner because they skip the step of unpacking a large saved package, but Windows and Apple machines still reuse theirs. The system still keeps smaller, faster-to-move caches for a few build steps and the helper tool itself, so those parts stay quick.

ai.title: Add freeDayUsed and freeDayLimit to subscription usage
ai.summary: Added `freeDayUsed` and `freeDayLimit` to `FreebuffSubscriptionUsage` in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts`. This exposes the caller's free premium-session pool for today, which clients cannot derive from `rateLimitsByModel` because it carries only the next-charged pool row, preventing double-counting once the free pool is exhausted. Both fields are optional, zero for quota-exempt accounts, and absent on older servers.

eli5.text: If you use the free trial sessions included with your subscription, you can now see exactly how many of today's free sessions you've used and how many you get total, right on your account screen. This only shows up for paying subscribers who get a free daily session pool, it stays blank on older servers that don't know about this feature, and stays zero if your account is exempt from limits. You don't need to change any settings for this; it just starts showing up whenever your service provider updates to the latest version that includes this field.
